What determines the direction a bolt of lightning will flow and how long it will continue until changing direction or branching?

In terms of the direction of the bolt, it has to do with the potential difference between the cloud and the ground/grounded object. This is assuming we are talking about ground-to-cloud lightning strikes. The most common lightning is Cloud to Cloud but it works essentially the same way.

During a storm, clouds build up a charge leaving them with an excess of ions. This creates a potential difference, much like the one between the ends of a battery. When these ions build up the electric field of the cloud can be thought of as feeling out for a way to neutralize its charge. Something like the Empire State building's lightning rod presents the easiest local path, so these charges will flow along the path between the rod and the cloud. Whenever lightning is striking, it is the attempt at reaching a local electrostatic equilibrium between the two points of the strike.

The branching is this same process happening at a much smaller scale. If you were to zoom in on a lightning bolt there would be many branches, like the veins of a leaf. It is the result this process of finding the easiest path to discharge ions occurring at multiple length scales simultaneously.

My son is 21, and took some time to do his own thing after high school. He's decided since awhile back that he wants to be an animator for TV shows. Relevant information: I’m a self-educated software developer, high school drop-out.

I’ve been guiding him in looking at the industry to see what skills will help him instead of grabbing a degree by the title and hoping for the best. After some conversations with a designer that I work with, he's pursuing a degree in advertising with a minor in fine arts.

I think he needs to look at the skill gap between what they’ll teach him and what the job will take and figure out what supplementary things he should study. I know how important skills are over educational titles from my own career, but I feel that he's still looking for a set of rails he can roll down with enthusiasm and verve, and end up with a job at the end.

How can I convince him to value skills over titles, and to consider his college as a piece of his education, not the corpus of it?
Education advice for my (young adult) son

My advice would be to encourage him to look for internships during the summer, so he can put what he learns at school to work. Yea you might not get paid for them, but that experience is everything when it comes to getting a job out of college. See if he can turn an summer internship into a year long thing; I've had a couple friends turn summer jobs into smaller side work during the school year

I think you absolutely hit the nail on the head with how important skills are over titles gained through education. It seems like you're doing everything right...but at some point he has to learn on his own. I agree with the encouragement towards an internship, which would be a fantastic experience for him but at the end of the day he'll need to blaze his own path.

Absolutely. I'm encouraging of his plan and I want him to know that my suggestions are suggestions, and that I don't think I can tell him what to do. I just have seen a lot of people pop out of college and think that their job application is just like another college application, when really, the reversal of the who-pays-who dynamic is just a night-and-day difference.

Especially considering the pursuit of artistic stuff. I love that he wants to create, I feel that it's what I do too even though I work with numbers and symbols instead of tablets and flash--and I also know that it amplifies the effect so much when you have to make a creative contribution instead of just following a script.
